conviction_note: Evidence roughly offsets: channel checks, October web traffic and a de-risked tape (-10.4% in 5 sessions on Anthropic-IPO rotation, no company news, ~2% SI) lean up; a billings gap vs consensus, a beat-small/raise-smaller guide pattern the stock sold in August (-7%), a CCaaS peer (Five9) sold -19.8% on its guide, and a 16-vol-point put skew lean down; impact_sum -0.1 and the scaled number +0.17 (p_up 51 x abs 8.5) agree on 'no edge'.
bar: Company Q3 FY27 guide revenue $1.275-1.280B, non-GAAP EPS $1.46-1.48, non-GAAP op income $510-515M (Q2 release, 2026-08-25, https://finviz.com/news/385449/zoom-communications-reports-financial-results-for-the-second-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2027); consensus $1.28B / $1.49 with whisper $1.55 (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-15, https://finviz.com/news/422873/zooms-enterprise-inflection-faces-its-next-test-as-white-label-churn-and-ai-costs-build); Citi $1.279B / $1.48, Q4 $1.297B / $1.55 (https://www.webull.com/news/15937106404099072). Guide and two estimate sources agree. Implied Q4 from FY guide $5.085-5.095B less Q1 $1,239.0M and Q2 $1,277.2M less Q3 guide = $1,288.8-1,303.8M (midpoint ~$1,296M, in line with Citi's $1.297B). Zoom beat the top of its revenue guide by $14M in Q1 and $7M in Q2, so a ~$1.287B print (+0.6% vs $1.28B) is the base case.
positioning_check: Short interest ~5.5M shares, ~1.9% of shares, 2.3 days to cover, down 11.8% m/m (Equibles, latest settlement ~mid-Nov 2026, https://equibles.com/stocks/zm/shortinterest); Massive: 6.24M, 2.1 days as of 2026-09-30. Not crowded, so no squeeze mechanism either way. Baseline: 25d skew +16.04 vol points (downside paid), event-implied move 7.04%, straddle 8.7%, ATM IV 93%, put/call OI 1.01; spot $86.21 is -10.37% over 5 sessions, -12.07% over 20, -22.9% from the 52w high. Sell side: 7 Buys/0 Sells, Citi PT 126->131 (11/17), Rosenblatt 130 and BTIG 115 (11/18) (Quiver, 2026-11-19).

findings.finding: Citi's channel-partner survey (published ~2026-11-17) found partners' Zoom-related product sales up 31% in FQ3 against their own 20-25% expectation, with Contact Center seen as a mid-market leader and AI Companion moving to paid tiers in H2; Citi's resulting revenue estimate $1.279B is at the top of the $1.275-1.280B guide and 'slightly above consensus' ($1.28B per Earnings Whispers rounding).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats above the top of guide are the norm here and have not paid: Q2 FY27 beat the top by $7M and raised FY EPS, stock -7.03% (2026-08-25); Q1 FY27 beat the top by $14M, stock +9.19% (2026-05-21). Mixed, so the reported-quarter line alone is not what decides the move.
findings.source_date: 2026-11-17 (page shows '6d ago'; Citi PT 131 dated 11/17/2026 by Quiver)
findings.why_not_priced: Partner survey is in one broker note, not in the wire consensus; if it were priced the stock would not have fallen 10% in five sessions with no estimate cuts, and consensus would sit above the guide top rather than at it. But it is a channel proxy with growth ~4% company-wide, so the dollars involved are small.
findings.independence: Shares one document with the web-traffic and billings findings (same Citi note). Different source pointing same way: RingCentral's 2026-10-22 subscriptions beat above the high end (https://www.ringcentral.com/whyringcentral/company/pressreleases/ringcentral-announces-third-quarter-2026-financial-results.html), filed separately.

findings.finding: Citi reports Zoom website visits improved about 2 points year over year in October 2026 'after a long post-pandemic decline', the first sign of top-of-funnel recovery in Online, the segment management cut to flat for FY27 in August citing weaker top-of-funnel traffic; Zoom also took ~6% list price increases across monthly and annual plans with online churn holding at 2.9% in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August 2026 cut of the Online outlook to flat was cited as a driver of the -7.03% reaction (finviz 2026-11-15 preview; invezz 2026-08-26). An Online stabilisation that lets management hold or lift the Online outlook is the reverse of the line that last sold the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: A single traffic datapoint in a broker note; consensus Online assumptions still reflect the August 'flat' cut. If priced, previews would expect an Online raise; the Nov 15 Earnings Whispers preview still frames Online as flat with weak traffic.
findings.independence: Same Citi note as finding 1. Price-increase and churn facts from the Q2 call summary (TradingKey, https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262131468-tradingkey). It is a proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: Citi flags billings as 'the largest gap' in the setup: it expects FQ3 billings of $1.230B against a consensus of $1.297B (-5%), consistent with the white-label contract churn management said would cut FY27 revenue growth ~40bp and enterprise ~60bp with more impact in H2; a billings/deferred-revenue shortfall headline is a plausible negative on a quarter where revenue is in line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of a billings-led reaction on ZM; the quality-of-beat lines (Online, margins) drove the -7.03% in August 2026 and -11.58% in Feb 2026 despite headline beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus billings sits at $1.297B per Citi, so the street has not marked down the line Citi expects to miss; the white-label headwind is guided but its billings timing is not. Citi also expects FCF above consensus ($549M vs $484M), which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: Same Citi note as findings 1-2. White-label headwind from the Q2 call summary (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262131468-tradingkey) and the Nov 15 preview (https://finviz.com/news/422873/zooms-enterprise-inflection-faces-its-next-test-as-white-label-churn-and-ai-costs-build), which estimates the drag at 40-60bp.

findings.finding: Enterprise growth may print below Q2's 7.8%: at Zoomtopia (2026-10-20) CFO Michelle Chang put enterprise growth in the latest quarter at 7.5%, and the guided white-label churn adds H2 drag; the market's FY2030 framing (6-8% total growth, double-digit enterprise) set at the same event raises the bar for the one segment that carries the story.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Enterprise acceleration to 7.8% (fastest in three years) did not prevent the -7.03% August reaction; the line has not paid on the upside, a deceleration is untested in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely inside guidance (white-label churn was guided), hence small; the 7.5% vs 7.8% discrepancy may be a definitional difference, which caps this finding.
findings.independence: Investor-day targets also reported by econotimes (https://econotimes.com/Zoom-Sets-6-to-8-Revenue-Growth-Goal-for-Fiscal-2030-1760014). White-label drag shares a source with finding 3.

findings.finding: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 (above the $70-78 range) and listed on 2026-11-19, closing day one at $97.17; Zoom's strategic investments were carried at $3,786M at 2026-07-31 after a $1,614M Q2 gain, and the stake was estimated at ~$3.9B at the $74 midpoint, so at $83-97 it is roughly $4.4-5.1B, about 17-20% of ZM's ~$25.6B market cap. The call is management's first chance to speak to the stake's value post-IPO and to capital allocation around it (the IPO mark itself falls in FQ4, after the Oct 31 quarter end).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Anthropic news has moved ZM hard outside prints (+11% on the 2026-06-01 IPO filing; +7.9% on 2026-11-11), but the $1.6B Q2 GAAP gain did not stop a -7.03% print reaction in August: the market treats the stake as a below-the-line asset, not an earnings item.
findings.why_not_priced: The IPO is public and ZM fell through it, so the stake's value is known; what is not priced is any management statement on monetisation or buyback after the 180-day lock-up. No path to the operating guide, so sized as a fraction.
findings.independence: Carrying value from Zoom's Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/385449/zoom-communications-reports-financial-results-for-the-second-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2027); stake estimate fourweekmba (https://fourweekmba.com/ai-spark-9-2b-zoom-3-9b-anthropic-backers-at-ipo-midpoint/); day-one close fourweekmba/CNBC (https://fourweekmba.com/ai-anthropic-closes-day-one-at-97-17-up-17-from-83-ipo/).

findings.finding: ZM fell from $98.08 (2026-11-11 close) to $86.21 into the print (-12%; -10.37% over 5 sessions) with no company news: StockStory (11/17) attributes the software slide to higher borrowing costs and 'Anthropic's upcoming listing giving institutions a direct public vehicle for AI exposure', and Quiver (11/19, -3.2% day) to positioning around the Anthropic debut; meanwhile three brokers raised or reiterated Buys on 11/17-18 and short interest is only ~1.9% of shares. The Anthropic-proxy premium has been taken out before the print, lowering the bar for the core business.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 print (+9.85%) came after a pre-print drift lower; Aug 2026 (-7.03%) came after a +4.8% run since the prior report and with the stock within 2.5% of its post-earnings high. The baseline has no explicit run-up-to-reaction mapping.
findings.why_not_priced: Sign is against a +16 vol-point put skew. Why the option market may be overpaying: the skew is struck after a rotation-driven 10% drop with realised vol at 60%, which itself inflates put demand; the drop's cause is named (direct ANT access), not an unknown fundamental, and estimates were raised not cut. Sized small because the skew is large.

findings.finding: Five9, the closest CCaaS peer, reported on 2026-11-05 (after Zoom last spoke) revenue +13% with CCaaS +8% and AI revenue +91%, beat estimates, and still fell 19.8% because next-quarter and FY EPS guidance missed consensus: demand in Zoom's growth segment is fine, but this group's reaction function in this tape is to sell guides that do not raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ZM's own August 2026 print (beat, small raise) fell 7.03%, the same shape.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer read and partly priced (ZM rose 7.9% on 11/11 after it); filed small as a reaction-function proxy, net of Zoom Contact Center being a minority of revenue.

findings.finding: RingCentral, the closest UCaaS peer, reported on 2026-10-22 subscriptions revenue +6.0% to $653M, above the high end of guidance, record margins, and raised FY2026 revenue to $2.650-2.657B and FCF to $620-630M: the UCaaS/phone demand environment through September was firm.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of ZM trading on RNG; reported-quarter beats on ZM have reacted both ways (+9.19%, -7.03%).
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a month and partly in the price; a peer proxy, so small. Its value is that it came after Zoom's August guide and before Zoom's quarter closed.
findings.independence: Citi's partner checks (finding 1) point the same way from a different source.

findings.finding: The dollar strengthened after Zoom set its Q3 guide on 2026-08-25 (which assumed constant-currency equal to reported): DXY gained more than 1.5% in September and ended October ~101.9, near 17-18-month highs, with yen and sterling leading G10 losses in October; Q2 carried a $2.7M FX tailwind (reported $1,277.2M vs $1,274.5M cc), so Q3 likely carries a small FX headwind of a few million dollars.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline; FX has not been a reaction driver for ZM.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (weekly recap; Trading Economics 2026-09-30 for the September gain)
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by the company; a few $M against a typical $7-14M beat over the guide top, so it trims the beat rather than flipping it.

findings.finding: At its 2026-10-20 Zoomtopia investor session Zoom set FY2030 targets of 6-8% revenue growth, ~40% non-GAAP operating margin and ~80% gross margin, committed to shrinking the share count in FY27 and beyond, and said $4.7B of buybacks were announced with $3.4B completed (~$1.3B authorization left at July 31; FY27 EPS guide excludes it); analysts raised FY28-29 enterprise estimates afterwards.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ratings and targets were raised 10/21-22 (Needham, Oppenheimer, RBC 130), so the event has been priced through the sell side; no print in the baseline has turned on buyback news.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced; it cuts both ways at this print: a new authorisation could come with the stake now liquid-in-prospect (up), while a FY27 Q4 guide near 4% growth sits visibly below the 6-8% target path (down). Netted to zero.
findings.independence: econotimes (https://econotimes.com/Zoom-Sets-6-to-8-Revenue-Growth-Goal-for-Fiscal-2030-1760014). Shares the marketscale document with finding 4.

findings.finding: Zoom's guidance habit is to beat the quarter and pass through less than the beat: Q2 FY27 beat the guide midpoint by ~$9.7M but FY27 revenue rose only $5M (to $5.085-5.095B), implicitly trimming H2 by ~$5M, and the implied Q4 ($1,288.8-1,303.8M, mid ~$1,296M) already sits on Citi's $1.297B, so a repeat leaves no Q4 raise for a tape that sold Five9's and Zoom's own non-raises.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: beat plus small raise plus Online cut to flat -> -7.03%. May 2026: beat by $14M with a FY raise -> +9.19%. The size of the pass-through has split the reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Arithmetic from the company's own releases (Q1 FY27 $1,239.0M per https://www.zawya.com/en/press-release/companies-news/zoom-communications-reports-financial-results-for-the-first-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2027-337838) that previews do not spell out; consensus Q4 equals the guide midpoint, leaving no cushion for a conservative Q4 guide.
findings.independence: Q1 release (zawya, above) and Citi Q4 estimate (https://www.webull.com/news/15937106404099072).

outside_window.finding: Zoom's Anthropic shares are presumably under the IPO's customary 180-day lock-up, so any monetisation or stake sale cannot happen before ~May 2027; the FQ4 GAAP gain on the IPO mark is reported with Q4 results in Feb/Mar 2027.

baseline_tension: Mostly agrees with the skew in the guidance-reaction findings and cuts against it in positioning (a rotation-driven 10% pre-print drop with ~2% short interest); net, the evidence offsets and p_up sits near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold its August beat-and-raise -7%): partner-checks finding cut +0.8 -> +0.5 and web-traffic finding +0.5 -> +0.4; p_up 53 -> 51.
Lesson 7 (sign against a +16 vol-point put skew): positioning finding cut +0.8 -> +0.5 and given an explicit why-the-skew-may-be-wrong sentence.
Lesson 2 (one-off with no path to the guide): Anthropic stake finding cut +0.5 -> +0.3, lock-up/IPO mark kept in outside_window.
Lesson 3/5 (caveat must reach the number; single-source broker estimate gap): billings finding cut -0.8 -> -0.6 because the same note expects FCF above consensus.
Left standing: enterprise, Five9, RingCentral, FX, investor-day and guidance-habit findings; abs_move_pct 8.5 unchanged (lesson 8 argues against shrinking it).
